tables.how: Payments to the Chinese Progressive Association and to the Center for Empowered Politics Education Fund (which the City’s tables spell “Center for Empowered Politics Education”), summed from the two tables with cents kept, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date. The association: fiscal 2019 $2,102,465.56, fiscal 2020 $2,094,299.67, fiscal 2021 $2,094,365.17, fiscal 2022 $1,765,244.19, fiscal 2023 $2,056,417.67, fiscal 2024 $1,998,137.05, fiscal 2025 $1,205,725.77, fiscal 2026 $768,211.42, fiscal 2027 $188,222.03 to date, in the table of every payment. The case’s $1,205,725.77 for fiscal 2025 and $1,998,137.05 for fiscal 2024 are these sums. The Education Fund: $245,950.68 in fiscal 2025, $219,005.08 in fiscal 2026 and $14,822.83 in fiscal 2027 to date, all from the Mayor’s office. No payment to a payee named Center for Empowered Politics (without “Education”), Resilient Strategies, Common Ground Fund or San Francisco Rising Action Fund is in the table of every payment: the only payee names matching those words are “CHINESE PROGRESSIVE ASSOCIATION”, “Center for Empowered Politics Education”. Each organization's payments in the two tables the Controller publishes, as retrieved on 12 November 2026: Citywide Nonprofit Spending, which by its own description keeps contracted services only, and Vendor Payments (Vouchers), the table of every payment. The fiscal year is the one printed on the payment. Payee names are matched by the rule the organization pages use: the name without punctuation and company suffixes, plus the renames and spellings that a shared contract number confirms.
tables.limits: City money is about a tenth of the association’s budget: its 2024 return reports $22,872,129 of revenue, $2,771,856 of it government grants from every government. These rows do not show what the money was spent on or who was paid from it; no record shows City grant money paying for campaign work. Fiscal 2027 had run four months when the tables were retrieved. A payment is money the City sent, not money the organization kept or spent on itself: subsidies, rent aid and grants that an organization pays on to others are in these figures. The two tables differ where the nonprofit-spending table leaves out a kind of payment or a contract; neither is wrong for that reason. The year printed on a payment can be later than the year the payment was issued. A payee the City spells in a way that no contract number ties to the organization is not counted.

The association’s 2024 return gives three amounts: $18,279,136 in the contractor list, $11,935,499 in the explanatory note and $11,404,687 on the management-fees line; its total expenses that year were $18,324,191, of which $1,179,000 were grants, so the contractor-list figure and the grants together ($19,458,136) are more than everything it spent. For 2022 and 2023 its notes give $8,667,060 and $10,129,549 but the contractor lists of those years do not name the company (largest listed: The Outreach Team $525,000 and SB Digital $1,979,698). The other two returns for 2024 also give more than one figure: the Center $692,594 in its contractor list and on its management-fees line but $629,594 in its note; the Education Fund $12,930,384 in its contractor list, $1,426,058 in its note and $1,457,455 on its management-fees line. The Education Fund’s return for 2023 enters $6,085,461 twice, as services and as reimbursement, against total expenses of $7,362,851; the case counts it once. The association’s returns for 2020 and 2021 do not name the company or report management fees. The returns spell the company “Resilient Strategies” and “Resilient Strategies LLC”; the schedules of related organizations give it one employer identification number, 84-3326035. The returns give the filer's name as “CHINESE PROGRESSIVE ASSOCIATION” and “Chinese Progressive Association”; they are one organization's by their employer identification number, 23-7404756. The returns give the filer's name as “CENTER FOR EMPOWERED POLITICS” and “The Center For Empowered Politics” and “The Center for Empowered Politics”; they are one organization's by their employer identification number, 45-3084134. The returns give the filer's name as “CENTER FOR EMPOWERED POLITICS EDUCATION FUND” and “Center for Empowered Politics Education” and “Center for Empowered Politics Education Fund”; they are one organization's by their employer identification number, 84-3636499.
tables.limits: The association’s 2024 return describes the arrangement as a managed services agreement under which the company supplies “worksite employees and administrative services as the statutory employer of record”, covering payroll, benefits, insurance, human resources and occupancy costs. An outside employer of record is a common way for a group of nonprofits to share payroll, and most of what is paid to one is staff pay. What reconciles the different figures is not on the returns; the largest may include costs the company paid on an organization’s behalf, and a figure may be a typing error. A line that does not name who was paid is marked as such and is not proof that the company was the payee. The three organizations’ payments are different organizations’ money and must not be added to each other or to the campaign payments. The case found no public statement from the association, the Center, the Education Fund or the company about these points in the records it reviewed. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. Its tax year is often not the City's fiscal year, and it counts money when earned or spent under its accounting method, not when the City paid. A disclosure on a return, including a dealing with an officer or a director, is what the law requires to be reported; the question is whether it is fair and approved.
